batch_engines.reason: Every indexed property receives the official mapped district, plan and design-district screens plus configured Appendix B dimensional rules. Geometry-backed activations calculate a bounded FAR/coverage envelope where the district has an unambiguous published rule; Section 5, uses, overlays, approvals, bonuses, variances and nonconformities remain controlling diligence.

Every assessor owner now receives a municipality-wide registry and active-UCC eligibility/result screen; business-like names are exact-matched against the official nightly Connecticut master, principal, agent, filing, and name-history datasets. Beneficial ownership and identity among similarly named parties remain unadjudicated.

Assessor-reported book/page, instrument code, party, price, and date observations are materialized as qualified recorded-document index evidence. The complete Stamford land-record index and deed instruments are not connected.

Every assessor owner now receives an official active-UCC/other-lien eligibility/result screen; matched records are linked as debtor-name observations. This is not a property-title, mortgage, assignment, release, judgment, or collateral adjudication.
Parcels are assembled by exact normalized situs address with explainable decisions; deed collateral, ownership adjacency, easements, and development-plan evidence are not yet used.

Every indexed property now receives a completed official master-development proximity screen. The City directs complete research across historical municipal records and its interactive OpenGov portal, which has no approved bulk interface.

Every indexed property now receives municipality-wide aquifer and coastal screens; geometry-backed activations add FEMA, EPA, wetlands, soils, elevation, structure, road, and risk-index screens. These are not environmental due diligence or a survey.

Every geometry-backed property receives official CTDEEP sewer-service-area and CTDPH community-water-service-area screens, City stormwater/access context, and Stamford WPCA system design-capacity context. These do not establish a parcel connection, main/lateral feasibility, pressure, fire flow, allocation, or reserved capacity.
